dedupe_keys.name: uk business disruption and economic losses from electricity failures and flooding koks et al 2019

description: This case study presents an integrated framework for estimating the economic impact of critical infrastructure failures and applies it to flooding in the United Kingdom. The framework combines geospatial information on infrastructure assets and networks and the hazards they face, geospatial modelling of how businesses rely on infrastructure services, and a multiregional supply-use model of the economy to trace wider effects of business disruption. The UK application uses the locations of electricity infrastructure assets and local industrial areas and follows the impacts of floods of different return periods across 37 subnational regions. It was written by Elco Koks, Raghav Pant, Scott Thacker and Jim Hall and published in the International Journal of Disaster Risk Science on 24 September 2019. Coverage is the United Kingdom by subnational region. The article is available free under CC BY 4.0, read here through its publisher metadata and abstract because the article page returned a browser challenge. Findings: counting power outages raised total economic losses by up to 300% compared with counting only flooded business premises, so risk studies that ignore infrastructure failure may underestimate losses. Caveats: the abstract does not give the loss values, data sources or model versions. For simulation it shows how flood exposure of substations cascades into business interruption and regional economic loss. It is related to the MRIA multiregional impact assessment model record in this catalogue.
